questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point particle is acted upon by a restoring force $- kx^{3}.$ The time period of oscillation is $T$ when the amplitude is $A.$ The time period for an amplitude $2A$ will be:
questions.solution:
Given $F = - k{x}^{3}$
$- \dfrac{dU}{dx} = - k{x}^{3}$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{1}{4}k{x}^{4}$
$∴$ Energy of oscillations will be
$E = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}k{x}^{4} \ldots \left(1\right)$
If we pull $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 0$ in above equation, we will
get amplitude as $A = \dfrac{4E}{k}4 \ldots \left(2\right)$

Also on rearranging equation $( 1 ) ,$ we get
$dt = \pm dx\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2E}}{\left(1 - \dfrac{k}{4E}{x}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2}$
Now, use $A = \dfrac{4E}{k}4 ,$ to reduce above equation
as $dt = \pm dx\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}{A}^{- 2}{\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{x}{A}\right)}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2}$
The time period can be found by integrating above equation.
$T = 4{∫}_{0}^{A}dx\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}{A}^{- 2}{\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{x}{A}\right)}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2}$

$= 4\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}{A}^{- 2}{∫}_{0}^{A}{\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{x}{A}\right)}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2} \cdot dx$
Put $\dfrac{x}{A} = u ⇒ dx = Adu$
$∴ T = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}{A}^{- 2} ( A ) {∫}_{0}^{1}du{\left(1 - {u}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2}$
$T = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}{A}^{- 1} ( I )$
Where $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}{\left(1 - {u}^{4}\right)}^{- 1 / 2}du$ is a numerical value
So from above equation $T ∝ {A}^{- 1}$
$∴ \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \dfrac{2A}{A} ⇒ {T}_{2} = \dfrac{T}{2}$

questions.q: Two masses $\mathrm{m}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}$ connected by a spring of spring constant $\mathrm{k}$ rest on a frictionless surface. If the masses are pulled apart and let go, the time period of oscillation is-
questions.solution: Let the masses be slightly displaced by $\mathrm{x}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{x}_{2}$ from this equilibrium position in opposite direction so net stretch in spring is $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{x}_{1}+\mathrm{x}_{2}$. Because of this a restoring force $\mathrm{kx}$ will act on each mass and therefore equation for $\mathrm{m}_{1} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{ m}_{2}$ will be $\mathrm{m}_{1} \frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{1}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=-\mathrm{kx} \quad \text{ and } \quad \mathrm{m}_{2} \frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{2}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=-\mathrm{kx}$ but as $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{x}_{1}+\mathrm{x}_{2}$ \therefore $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{1}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}+\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{2}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}$ replacing values of $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{1}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}$ and $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{2}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}$ from acceleration equations we get $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}_{2}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=-\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}_{1}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}_{2}}\right) \mathrm{kx}$ also if $\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}_{1}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}_{2}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}}$ then $\mathrm{m}$ is the effective mass in this case therefore $\frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=-\omega^{2} \mathrm{x}=\frac{-\mathrm{kx}}{\mathrm{m}}$ or $\omega^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}$ \therefore $\sqrt{\Gamma=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m_{1} m_{2}}{\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right) k}}}$

questions.q: A book is resting on shelf that is undergoing vertical simple harmonic oscillations with an amplitude of $2.5 \mathrm{ cm}$. What is the minimum frequency of oscillation of the shell for which the book will lose contact with the shelf $?$ (Assume that $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrms^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
Book will loose contact with the shelf when $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g}$.
Now $|\mathrm{a}|=\omega^{2} \mathrm{x} \therefore \mathrm{g}=\omega^{2} \mathrm{ A} \quad(\mathrm{ A} \rightarrow$ Amplitude) $\begin{array}{l} \omega^{2}=\frac{g}{A}\text{ also } f=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi}\\
\therefore f=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{g}{A}}
\end{array}$ replacing $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{ m}/ \mathrms^{2}$ and $\mathrm{A}=$2.5 \times 10^{-2} $\mathrm{ m}$
We get $\mathrm{f}=$3.18 $\mathrm{ Hz}$
